storage_source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers CWMS Data API, Pacific Northwest Region office (NWDP)
capacity_source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers National Inventory of Dams. This provider publishes no full level in acre-feet -- its pools are defined by elevation -- so ADR-070 never fires and ADR-003 with ADR-072 decides every denominator (ADR-102).
selection: Every storage-bearing location under the NWDP office, audited with tools/audit_cwms_stations.py on 2026-08-30: one series chosen per location by the stated preference and confirmed by a read, then the shared screens in admission.py. 12 admitted on confirmed dam matches, 24 withheld with the finding behind each. 73 further locations are already published within 3 km through another provider and are deduplicated rather than withheld (ADR-069); their location ids are listed below. Names are reviewed display names, not the service's gauge labels (ADR-079).

ALF.name: Lake Pend Oreille
ALF.finding: The series is total lake storage for Lake Pend Oreille, a natural lake whose last few feet Albeni Falls Dam regulates: 1,557,900 acre-feet observed against the dam's 1,153,000 conservation pool and 1,155,000 maximum. The reading is the lake, not the storage the dam holds, so dividing one by the other would publish a percentage of the wrong quantity. Needs a usable-storage series, or the successor ADR-078 anticipates for a water measured as a lake.

BON.name: Bonneville Pool
BON.finding: 745,300 acre-feet observed against Bonneville's 277,000 conservation pool and 537,000 maximum -- 39% above the largest figure the inventory names. The reported storage is the whole reach behind the dam rather than a pool the record describes. Held under the no-repair rule: no source here says which figure to believe.

COEI.name: Coeur d'Alene Lake
COEI.finding: Coeur d'Alene Lake, a natural lake whose outlet is regulated by Post Falls Dam about 20 km downstream; no dam stands within the matching radius, and the inventory publishes no storage figure this series could be divided by. ADR-078 admits a water on its dam, and this one needs the successor that record anticipates.

PRD.name: Priest Rapids Lake
PRD.finding: A mid-Columbia run-of-river pool operated within a few feet. The inventory's pool figure describes the reach behind the dam while the pool itself swings a small fraction of it, so a percent of full would be true and useless -- which is the finding the never-filled screen exists to make (ADR-102). Measured: never seen a third full: 43,561 acre-feet observed against 191,000, 23%.
